For over thirty years our drive and passion to change the world has enabled us to become the largest producer and marketer of bioethanol and a leader in sustainable products in the world. PERKS A multifaceted wellness program encompassing the whole person – mentally, physically, and spiritually 'Family-first' culture On-site fitness centers or fitness reimbursements JOB SUMMARY RESPONSIBILITIES The Plant Engineering Intern works closely with the Plant Manager and the Maintenance Manager to maximize efficiencies of plant operations while optimizing plant run time. The Plant Engineering Intern troubleshoots and identifies process needs to maintain production levels and assists in the development of predictive and preventative maintenance programs. This is an on-site role located in Corning, IA . Some or all of the following projects/research/initiatives relating to plant operations may be assigned throughout the duration of the internship: Efficiencies Maintenance Process Optimization Operations Compile Analyze data Location-specific research Environmental Compliance Additional responsibilities include: Work with the Plant Manager and Maintenance Manager on operation/troubleshooting issues, as well as efforts to review and enhance predictive maintenance programs. Work with the maintenance department and outside vendors to assist in the ongoing development of the preventative maintenance program. The Plant Engineering Intern will determine applicable equipment, necessary tools, and required inspection frequencies. Work with the management team to further strengthen and develop plant operating procedures. Maintain confidentiality relating to projects and processes. Foster a culture of safe behavior and environmental compliance at all times. Maintain a team environment at all times and champion POET in the community. Maintain and advance the food safety and quality of POET’s products and processes to deliver a best-in-class culture of quality. Since we’re all about teamwork and getting the job done, your skills may be put to a lot of other uses! The POET Never Satisfied Internship openings are for Summer 2027. We post Internships in early September with the intention of having interns selected by November 1st. QUALIFICATIONS SKILLS High school diploma or equivalent, required. Junior or Senior-level student enrolled full-time at an accredited 4-year college/university pursuing a degree in Chemical, Mechanical, or Agricultural Engineering. Must be able to work a variety of shifts, minimum of 40 hours/week. Excellent organizational, time management, and communication skills, as well as the ability to adapt to change Knowledge of the basics of the Microsoft Office Suite and the ability to learn new programs. Bonus points : familiarity or experience with DCS control and DCS historian systems A SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE High level of personal integrity Interpersonal skills – ability to effectively interact with individuals at all levels within/outside the organization Demonstrated problem-solving and critical thinking skills Ability to embrace and promote change Innovative mindset Ability to think objectively Self-awareness in the face of uncertainty Ability to work in a team environment PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS This role has some physical requirements that our team members will need to be able to perform, such as: Occasionally lifting weight up to sixty (60) pounds. Climbing several flights of stairs and ladders. Opening valves. Occasionally bending, twisting and turning while lifting weight of less than fifty (50) pounds. Data entry while seated for greater than one (1) hour. Walking up to two (2) or more miles per day Pushing brooms, shovels, etc. Working at heights, in confined spaces and at temperatures from -20 to +100 degrees. Standing for extended periods of time. WORK ENVIRONMENT Occasional travel will be part of the norm for this position. At times, overnight travel may be required. Team members will be required to adhere to all safety requirements at all times and in all work environments. This position is exposed to work in multiple environments, including plant, laboratory, as well as an office environment. The team member may be exposed to high noise levels, moving mechanical parts, dusty conditions, internal and external temperature/weather conditions, and chemicals. We have frequent team events, volunteer efforts, and we know how to celebrate wins! Sodium-Ion is cheap, readily available and safe, making it the leading contender in a rapidly evolving market. Our leadership team is powered by decades of expertise in scaling gigawatt-level innovation at world-class companies such as Tesla, Northvolt, Apple, Powin, Enovix, Zipline, Solid Power, and Fluence. We are backed by strategic investment and product partners such as TDK Ventures and Eclipse Ventures. We are a team of engineers, operators, entrepreneurs, and partners driven by a shared ambition to set the new performance standard for renewable energy and grid resilience. About the Role – Systems Integration and Test Engineering Intern This intern will support integration testing and functional verification of Peak Energy's energy storage systems, working across BMS, inverters, and other systems from batteries to power electronics. As Peak Energy scales its ESS testing infrastructure, this role helps build out the benchtop and HIL test capabilities needed to validate systems ahead of production. You'll work closely with firmware, design, and simulation teams, gaining exposure to the full test lifecycle – from procedure development to execution to reporting. This role suits a hands-on, curious engineer who's eager to learn by doing and comfortable navigating ambiguity in a fast-moving startup environment. What You'll Do (Responsibilities) Support functional testing of BMS, inverters, and other systems across Peak Energy's energy storage product Help design, set up, and run benchtop and HIL test setups for validation of the BMS Develop and execute test scripts to support test automation efforts Assist in developing test plans and procedures across electrical and mechanical systems Interface with design, simulation, and manufacturing engineering partners to inform design decisions Help analyze test data and document findings for engineering teams Support troubleshooting and diagnosis of issues identified during testing Participate in a culture of rapid prototyping and testing What You'll Bring (Qualifications) Pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a closely related field Experience interfacing with microcontrollers and writing scripts for functional testing Basic familiarity with electromechanical test setups Proficiency in Python or similar Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Comfortable working hands-on with hardware and lab equipment Passion for renewable energy, sustainability, and driving positive environmental impact through technology innovation Eligible to work in the U.S. Preferred Qualifications Exposure to high voltage battery and power electronics systems Familiarity with battery management systems (BMS) architecture Coursework or project experience with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test systems Peak Energy is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce.
